Attendance

The register, marked in the classroom

A teacher opens their class on a phone, taps the two or three children who are not there, and presses save. That is the whole interaction, and it has to be faster than the paper register or it will not be used.

Start 14 day free trial Read the handbook

It keeps working when the connection does not

This is the part most software gets wrong, and the part that decides whether teachers keep using it in week three.

Marked offline, queued, then synced

A register marked with no signal is saved on the phone and sent when there is one. The teacher is told which state it is in rather than left guessing, and the same class cannot be marked twice into two different answers.

Finalise and lock the day

An unfinalised register is a draft and says so. Once the day is finalised it is locked, so a figure quoted to a parent in the afternoon is the same figure next week. A correction after that is a recorded change, not a silent overwrite.

Teachers see only their own classes

A teacher login reaches the classes and subjects that teacher actually teaches, and nothing else. That is enforced in the database rather than by hiding a menu, so it holds even if somebody types a different address.

The printable monthly sheet

The sheet an inspector or a board asks for, printed from the same data the teachers marked, so it cannot disagree with itself. Present, absent, late, half day and leave are all separate states.

Attendance is also a fee control

A pupil who is on the fee roll but has never appeared in any attendance register is worth looking at. That is not an accusation, it is usually a pupil who left and was never marked as gone, and it is money the school thinks it is owed by a family that has moved on.

The reconciliation screen puts those two lists side by side and names the difference, which is a check no paper register can do at all.
